title: Beyond Correlation: A Causality-Driven Machine Learning Framework to Climate-Crop Yield Data Using Transfer Entropy and Lag Optimization Approaches
summary: Transfer entropy screened climate variables and lags, and regressors predicted maize and soybean yields from 40 years of USDA-NASS data for 88 Ohio counties. The held-out results describe observational climate-yield associations; a random split does not establish causality or broad geographic transfer.
ai_technology: Transfer entropy feature screening and lag selection; machine-learning yield regressors
organization: Not stated in the abstract reviewed

evidence.tested: On 3,360 Ohio county-years, held-out random-split prediction reported R² of about 0.75 for maize and 0.72 for soybean, with selected climate variables and lags.
evidence.unknown: The analysis is observational and county-year dependent; no temporal or geographic external validation is reported.
evidence.ai_role: Transfer entropy feature screening and lag selection; machine-learning yield regressors

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
